purpose: Ranolazine is used to treat chronic chest pain called angina. It helps reduce how often you get chest pain episodes so you can be more active in your daily life. It is usually used when other angina medicines have not worked well enough on their own.
how_it_works: Your heart muscle cells sometimes get overloaded with sodium, which can cause them to work too hard and lead to chest pain. Ranolazine blocks a specific channel that lets too much sodium into heart cells, helping the heart muscle relax and work more efficiently. This reduces the strain on your heart without significantly slowing your heart rate or lowering your blood pressure.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are dizziness, headache, constipation, and nausea. Some people also feel tired or notice a spinning sensation. These effects are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as ranolazine may not be safe for you. It can cause a change in your heart's electrical activity called QT prolongation, so let your doctor know if you take other medicines that affect heart rhythm. Avoid grapefruit juice, as it can increase the level of this drug in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Do not crush or chew the tablets — swallow them whole.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 500 mg taken by mouth twice a day, once in the morning and once in the evening. Your doctor may increase this to 1000 mg twice a day if needed and if you are tolerating the medicine well. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, with or without food.
